entry.evidence: The geodynamic setting of the Namaqua Sector during Mesoproterozoic times has long been debated with two main hypotheses proposed.

steps.action: Pose the long-debated question of the Mesoproterozoic geodynamic setting of the Namaqua Sector, with the Kakamas Domain as the key area to resolve it.
steps.quote: The geodynamic setting of the Namaqua Sector during Mesoproterozoic times has long been debated with two main hypotheses proposed.

steps.action: Name the two rival published models: a Namaqua Wilson-cycle accretion/collision model and a long-duration back-arc model (Bial et al. 2015b; Büttner 2020).
steps.quote: The second model contends that the observed high-T, low-P (<6 kbar) metamorphism argues against the excessive crustal thickening of continental collision tectonics

steps.action: Use 1:50,000 transfrontier mapping and field data to define a unified lithostratigraphy (new Ham River and Komsberg suites), redefine the SW boundary of the domain, and describe the D2-D4 structural history.
steps.quote: Despite its size, the lithostratigraphy of the central and NW Kakamas Domain is relatively simple

steps.action: Infer peak P-T conditions of four Narries metapelites by THERMOCALC pseudosection modelling of XRF bulk compositions; result is about 4.5-5.3 kbar and 770-790 °C at the solidus.
steps.quote: constrain peak metamorphism at 4.5–5.3 kbar

steps.action: Check that the four pseudosections from different areas give the same topology and peak field.
steps.quote: The topology of all four calculated pseudosections is very similar

steps.action: Date 26 samples by U-Pb zircon (LA-ICP-MS, SHRIMP) to fix detrital, metamorphic and emplacement ages of paragneisses, orthogneisses and Komsberg Suite; check ages against intrusive relations.
steps.quote: Zircons from 26 samples were dated

steps.action: Analyse 134 igneous samples for major and trace elements and 16 for Sm-Nd isotopes, supplemented with published analyses.
steps.quote: 134 representative samples of the igneous rocks of the central and NW Kakamas Domain were analysed for major and trace elements

steps.action: Use the coherent Harker trends to confirm the field-based grouping of the Komsberg Suite, a second method on the mapped units.
steps.quote: confirms their grouping into a suite based on field characteristics, mineralogy and age data

steps.action: Compare Narries detrital zircon spectra with crystallisation and xenocryst ages of adjacent domains; infer the domains were juxtaposed before deposition at about 1220 Ma.
steps.quote: it also implies that the Kakamas Domain must have been in proximity to the other tectonic components of the Namaqua Sector

steps.action: Merge the Arribees Group and Kenhardt units into a single Narries Group on the basis of similar detrital age spectra.
steps.quote: we propose that the Arribees Group be abandoned

steps.action: Infer an S-type parentage of the 1210-1190 Ma Eendoorn and Ham River suites, with Narries metapelites and older Paleoproterozoic crust as sources.
steps.quote: all point to an S-type granite parentage

steps.action: Reject the mapping team's earlier view that the Witwater Gneiss crystallised from Narries leucosome melts, because most samples date about 60-80 Myr after Narries metamorphism.
steps.quote: The residual Narries Group metapelites seem an unlikely candidate source for the younger Witwater Gneiss

steps.action: Infer the petrogenesis of the Komsberg Suite (I- and A2-type signals) as mixed crustal sources with mantle input.
steps.quote: derivation of the Komsberg Suite from a mix of crustal source regions with significant mantle input

steps.action: Combine new and published ages into an events-time synthesis of the Namaqua Sector from about 2.0 Ga to 960 Ma.
steps.quote: The following discussion aims to provide a tentative outline of the progressive evolution of the Namaqua Sector

steps.action: State the expectations of hot versus cold orogen end-members from the literature: thickening, high-P, clockwise paths and strain localisation versus sustained high-T/low-P and pervasive flow.
steps.quote: cold orogens show typically clockwise P-T-t paths, evidence of high-P metamorphism

steps.action: Compare the Namaqua record (uniform high-T/low-P over >200,000 km2 for >100 Myr, pervasive low-angle fabrics) with the hot-orogen expectations.
steps.quote: the Namaqua Sector combines many, if not all, of the hallmark features of a

steps.action: Argue against the accretionary model, which cannot explain long-lived low-P metamorphism, the lack of juvenile Nd signatures, the detrital proximity and the fabric orientation.
steps.quote: this model fails to adequately explain the long duration of the high-T, low P (<6 kbar) metamorphism

steps.action: Take from modern Cordilleran and Andean back-arc studies the expectation of hot, thin back-arc lithosphere with mantle-coupled crustal flow.
steps.quote: indicate anomalously hot and thin back-arc lithosphere that may extend for hundreds of kilometres behind the volcanic arc

steps.action: Read the facing of the Bushmanland sheath folds as bottom-to-NE underthrusting, consistent with bottom-driven crustal flow.
steps.quote: The orientation and facing of the sheath folds thus indicate a bottom-to-the-NE underthrusting of the crustal package.

steps.action: Keep the back-arc setting as the explanation, concurring with Bial et al. and Büttner.
steps.quote: we concur with the general sentiment of Bial et al. (2015a,b, 2016) and Büttner (2020) of the regional setting of Namaqualand in a back-arc realm

steps.action: Refine the back-arc model into a three-stage evolution (1210-1120, 1120-1100, 1100-1030 Ma) driven by slab retreat.
steps.quote: We contend that the available data can best be explained by the following three stage evolution

steps.action: Set the model against other long-duration mid-Proterozoic hot orogens (Eastern Ghats, Napier, Sveconorwegian back-arc).
steps.quote: very similar to that proposed here for the Namaqua Sector

end.claim: The Namaqua Sector is a long-lived hot orogen developed in a wide continental back-arc, with subduction west of the present outcrop, rather than an accretion-collision belt.

decisive_move.sentence: The pseudosection estimate of uniform low-P/high-T peak conditions (about 5 kbar, about 780 °C), combined with the ages showing these conditions lasted from 1210 to 1110 Ma, is what makes the over-thickening required by the collision model untenable.

gates.evidence: Action: the data came from a regional mapping program aimed at a unified lithostratigraphy (p. 3), though the study is framed as able to resolve the impasse between the two models (p. 3). Claim: the P-T estimates could have shown high pressures and the isotopes juvenile input, but the verdict rests on qualitative consistency with literature end-members, not on a crucial test. Registration: nothing is reported as fixed before the data were seen.

Internally consistent thermodynamic dataset and THERMOCALC phase-equilibrium computation

present a new geodynamic model for the Namaqua Sector as a whole
the two members from the Grünau-Ai-Ais region (Fig. 3) are newly recognized

limits:
Sub-claims and their statuses:
- Peak P-T of 4.5-5.3 kbar and 770-790 °C: estimate_with_resolution.
- Narries deposition between about 1260 and 1215 Ma, and the U-Pb ages: estimate_with_resolution.
- Unified lithostratigraphy and merged Narries Group: kept as best_explanation from correlation.
- Origin of the Witwater Gneiss: unresolved; the alternative sources are not tested.
- Role of the Umkondo plume: left open.

Process limits:
- The back-arc verdict is argued by consistency with literature end-members and modern analogues. No quantitative thermal or geodynamic model of the rival predictions is computed here.
- The sheath-fold and Bushmanland evidence is taken from cited work.
- Nothing is reported on the order of fieldwork, dating and interpretation beyond the revised Witwater interpretation. The extent of iteration is inference.
- Pseudosection parameter choices (Fe3+ fixed at 10% of total Fe, H2O set at the solidus) are stated but not varied.
- No review file was supplied, although the acknowledgements name three reviewers.
- The XML text had no body paragraphs, so section/paragraph locators could not be used.
